Saudi state owned oil giant Saudi Aramco has told employees to evacuate its headquarters campus in Dhahran and work remotely. Unclear for how long. Oil production remains unchanged, but clearly the kingdom sees a greater Houthi risk.

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue. Riyadh disclosed that two contractors were killed in a drone attack that targeted the giant Shaybah oilfield (in the Empty quarter region near the UAE border). Another person died on an attack against the Dammam airport, near the country’s top oil installations in the Eastern province.

US crude oil exports to Asia are set to hit multi-year lows after the Iran war disrupted global shipping and pushed the cost to lease a tanker for the Pacific journey to a record of almost $80 million.

Asian refinery orders for US crude for delivery in November tumbled roughly 50% to 24 million to 26 million barrels this month sequentially, according to traders. If that pace of orders holds through the end of this month, it would mark a seven-year low, based on ship-tracking data from Kpler and Vortexa

AI jitters hit copper, Middle East tensions lift oil, and gold struggles despite ETF inflows. Meanwhile, grains unwind crowded longs. Why commodities remain attractive as a portfolio hedge, with supply risks and positive roll returns in focus.
#Commodities #Oil #Gold #Copper https://t.co/gXYhqMSMPW via @saxobank

What a morning across markets:

Nasdaq tumbles +500 points amid continued AI-related jitters.

Copper drops 2.2% on uncertainty over whether the US will impose tariffs on refined copper, compounded by concerns about a potential slowdown in AI and data centre investment.

Crude oil reaches a five-month high above USD 112 as heightened Middle East tensions and risk of US attacks fuel fears of further supply disruptions.

Gold struggles below USD 4,100 despite softer Treasury yields and a slightly weaker dollar.

European bonds: The French 10-year government bond yield rises above 5% for the first time in 24 years, highlighting mounting concerns over the country's fiscal outlook. The spread to Germany jumps to near 170 bps, highest ever.

Key takeaways from EIAs weekly report.
US crude and gasoline inventories both fell by around 3 million barrels, with the latter dropping to its lowest seasonal level since 2014. Distillate stocks, meanwhile, rose by 1.6 million barrels after hitting a record seasonal low, probably supported by a 0.6 mb/d sharp drop in demand to 3.7 mb/d

Refineries operated at 93% of capacity, the highest seasonal utilisation rate since 1997, while crude processing reached a record seasonal high.

US crude production slumped by 0.4 mb/d to 13.27 mb/d as Hurricane Isaias forced temporary shut-ins, while exports fell for a second week to a one-month low at 3.4 mb/d.

Commodities:

Oil: Brent trades back above USD 111 a barrel, up 2%, after a deadly drone strike on Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah field which left operations unaffected, while a separate attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one. Both incidents highlight the risk of further escalation that could disrupt supply. Prices whipsawed again on Wednesday following another unsubstantiated report of a potential Qatar-Pakistan peace proposal. Meanwhile, the EIA reported a hurricane Isaias-related weekly drop of 0.4 mb/d in US crude production. Distillate inventories recovered from a record seasonal low, while gasoline stocks fell to their lowest level since 2014. Both gasoil and ULSD (HO) remain near USD 200 a barrel, highlighting continued tightness in refined-product markets.

Metals: Spot gold fell 1.3% to around USD 4,090 an ounce as rising energy prices added to inflation and interest-rate concerns, triggering further speculative selling. This pressure has only been partly offset by continued ETF demand, with Bloomberg data showing an 11.4-tonne increase in holdings this week to a fresh four-year high. The key question now is whether gold can find support below USD 4,100 for a third time this month, or whether we may witness a sustained break. Silver dropped 3% to USD 56.20, while copper slipped 1.5% to USD 6.48 a pound.

The South American nation of Guyana first began exporting crude oil in January 2020. Production takes place offshore at four locations, with a fifth about to be introduced.

Exports are stated in thousands of barrels per day:

2020: 76
2021: 106
2022: 267
2023: 381
2024: 599
2025: 706
2026: 879

Top destinations are USA (28%), Netherlands (20%), Italy (7%), Spain (6%) and UK (5%), but there are nearly three dozen nations on the list.
